method: Opened current official Git, Python 3.12 and GitHub Actions documentation through the web tool; inspected relevant command, environment, hash, context and event sections. No GitHub account, remote repository or hosted workflow was accessed.
originality: All eight lesson narratives, fictional scenarios, 24 questions, code fixtures, safety contract and handoff rubric are original teaching. Sources support narrow command/library/CI facts, not the pedagogical design or a claim of certification coverage.
versionScope: Execution target: installed Git 2.52.0 and Python 3.12.14 on Linux. Python documentation currently labels 3.12.16; stable APIs used. Current Git reference pages can describe newer options; the lab uses only the bounded operations actually verified here. Other platforms/versions are not certified.

sources.title: Git glossary
sources.supports: Working tree, index, HEAD, commit, branch, parent and fast-forward vocabulary.

sources.title: Git add reference
sources.supports: Staged contents select the next plain commit; later edits require another add.

sources.title: Git diff reference
sources.supports: Ordinary working-tree/index comparison versus cached index/HEAD comparison.

sources.title: Git status reference
sources.supports: Porcelain/short status and distinct staged, unstaged and untracked states.

sources.title: Git commit reference
sources.supports: Commit information and author/committer fields; author name does not affect authentication.

sources.title: Git branch reference
sources.supports: Branch-head creation at a revision and branch/reference behavior.

sources.title: Git merge reference
sources.supports: Fast-forward versus true merge, conflicts and explicit edit/add/commit resolution.

sources.title: Git revert reference
sources.supports: Additive corrective commits reversing changes; clean-state requirement and nontrivial cases.

sources.title: Git show reference
sources.supports: Inspecting committed objects and file contents.

sources.title: Git rev-parse reference
sources.supports: Resolving exact revision identities; verification syntax and ambiguity precautions.

sources.title: Git configuration reference
sources.supports: Configuration scopes, author metadata, hooks, signing and helper settings.

sources.title: Git command and environment reference
sources.supports: GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM/GLOBAL/NOSYSTEM and environment variables that affect execution.

sources.title: Git init reference
sources.supports: Repository initialization, explicit initial branch/object format and template selection.

sources.title: Python 3.12 tempfile
sources.supports: Owned temporary directories/files and ordinary context-manager cleanup.

sources.title: Python 3.12 subprocess
sources.supports: Argument lists, explicit environment, shell=False, return codes and timeout behavior.

sources.title: Python 3.12 unittest
sources.supports: Standard-library assertions, tests, discovery and subtests.

sources.title: Python 3.12 hashlib
sources.supports: SHA-256 computation over bytes and hexadecimal digest representation.

sources.title: GitHub Actions workflow events reference
sources.supports: pull_request can test the merge-branch commit rather than only the contributor head.

sources.title: GitHub Actions contexts reference
sources.supports: github.sha identifies a workflow-triggering commit with event-dependent meaning.

sources.title: GitHub Actions artifact attestations
sources.supports: Signed provenance claims are distinct from an unauthenticated local digest; no attestation implemented here.
